close_reason: Not a bug: two-way name_matches_subtree is correct for semantic equality detection. Reviewer confirmed this in the issue description.
description:
**Issue**: At lib.rs:2025-2029, the excludedSubtrees deduplication uses a two-way `name_matches_subtree` check to determine if two entries are 'the same subtree':

```rust\nlet already_present = nc_excluded.iter().any(|existing| {\n    same_nc_variant(&existing.base, &new_entry.base)\n        && name_matches_subtree(&existing.base, new_entry)\n        && name_matches_subtree(&new_entry.base, existing)\n});\n```

The two-way match (A matches B AND B matches A) is correct for *exact* subtree equality but fails to deduplicate cases where one subtree is a strict subset of another. For example, if nc_excluded already contains '.example.com' and a CA adds '.sub.example.com', these are NOT bi-directionally matching (sub.example.com ⊂ example.com, not equal), so both entries are kept. This is semantically correct for RFC 5280: a more-specific excluded entry is not redundant with a less-specific one; the exclusion list is a union of all excluded regions.

**However**: The code comment at line 2021 says 'two entries are considered the same subtree when each matches the other (i.e., they are semantically equivalent, not just byte-equal).' This is the right framing. The two-way check correctly identifies exact duplicates. Supersets and subsets are correctly NOT deduplicated.

**The actual subtle issue**: For DNS names, `name_matches_subtree(existing, new_entry)` asks 'does existing.base match the constraint new_entry?' — i.e., is existing.base within new_entry's subtree? So the two-way check asks: 'is A within B AND is B within A?' For DNS, this means both are the same hostname or subdomain relationship is symmetric — which for finite-depth subtrees only holds when they're equivalent.

For DirectoryName, `dn_within_subtree` checks prefix containment. Two-way containment means they share an exact common prefix of equal length, which again means they're equal (both have the other as a prefix → same length → same DN). This IS correct for equality detection.

**Resolution**: The two-way check is semantically correct for deduplication. No bug. But add a comment explaining WHY two-way is correct (mutual containment implies equality for these name types) to prevent future readers from 'optimizing' it to one-way.\n\n**Location**: pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2025-2029\n\n**Severity**: P4 (documentation only — the code is correct but confusing)
title: nc_excluded dedup uses two-way subtree match — semantically wrong
